rationale: CSS backdrop-filter was a scalar blur radius end to end. The canvas exposed only save_backdrop_filter(x, y, w, h, blur_radius), so saturate(), brightness(), invert(), grayscale(), sepia(), contrast(), hue-rotate() and any composition of them were parsed and discarded, and a design that desaturates what is behind an element rendered it at full saturation. Adds Canvas::save_backdrop_filter_chain taking the same FilterChainEntry list the foreground filter chain already used, with a default that sums blur entries and drops the rest so every existing backend keeps exactly the behaviour it had; a new CanvasCapability::backdrop_filter_chain lets a caller tell the two apart rather than infer faithfulness. The Skia override reuses the element-layer chain builder, now extracted as compose_css_filter_chain, so the two layers cannot drift into disagreeing about what saturate(0.15) means. The one non-obvious part is the crop: SkImageFilters::ColorFilter reports unbounded output, so saveLayer treats its bounds as a hint and grows the layer to the device clip, and the filtered result then composites over everything already painted -- the whole panel floods with one colour. The composed chain is therefore wrapped in SkImageFilters::Crop; cropping only the blur entry, which is what the blur-only path did because a blur was the only unbounded thing it could produce, is not sufficient. This is the same unbounded-output trap already documented one function away for the crt shader effect. Measured against Chrome on a probe design that uses these filters, area-weighted failing fraction improves 0.3220 to 0.0035 with ink coverage 0.9986 to 0.9994; no design in the current corpus declares a non-blur backdrop-filter, so the corpus numbers are unchanged. drop-shadow() in a backdrop list and url(#filter) remain unsupported and are named as such in the ledger. Pulp-only: the gap and the fix both originate here, with no counterpart framework change to backport.
